13827.title: Is there any way to stop any Google News Stories
13827.note: news.google.com/rss/articles/<token> links redirect to consent.google.com from NewsBlur's EU servers and the consent page was extracted as story text. Fix: Feed.resolve_google_redirect_url decodes the token via MStory._decode_google_news_url; TextImporter refuses consent.google.com; fetch_original_text drops cached consent text. Verified decoder works from happ-web-01. Reply assumes deploy (make deploy + make celery).
13827.reply: JTTraveler is right that Google News feeds only carry a headline and a link, but that cookie notice was on NewsBlur's side. Google News links go through a news.google.com redirect, and when NewsBlur's servers, which sit in Europe, followed it to pull the article text, Google handed them its cookie consent page instead of the story. That page is what ended up as the text. I've fixed it so NewsBlur decodes the link to the real article first and never keeps that consent page as a story's text. Stories that already show the notice will swap in the real article the next time you open them.

13844.note: edmcfadden is uid 657056, paid premium to 2027-09-19, 84 subs, 745 starred stories, client is ReadKit. The 429 is the @ratelimit(minutes=5, requests=50, use_path=True) on load_starred_stories in apps/reader/views.py (added 54c60c1a2 2025-01-21, no rationale; use_path added 45331c005 2025-04-11). Django logs from all six happ-web servers (2026-09-21 23:09Z to 2026-09-22 04:38Z): 1200 'Loading starred stories: 10 stories' lines, 143 load_feeds, 155 starred_story_hashes, 155 unread_story_hashes. Successful starred loads peak at exactly 49 per rolling 6-minute window (the cap), and ReadKit re-syncs every 60-90s. IP limiter (500/5min, IP_RATE_LIMITING_ENABLED) and load_feeds (60/min) are nowhere near tripping. Live redis-user db 6: 35 starred rl- counters, 1 at the cap. Could not confirm page= vs h= because no prod log carries query strings (hwww haproxy logs to 127.0.0.1 syslog but rsyslog imudp is disabled; happ-web haproxy logs nothing; SigNoz MCP is not a NewsBlur workspace). Sam's decisions 2026-09-22: draft an email to the ReadKit developer (support@readkit.app) asking for hash-diff sync, limit=100, and 429 backoff; then also open PR #2146 raising load_starred_stories to 100/5min and adding Retry-After to both 429 emitters (utils/ratelimit.py decorator computes seconds until enough one-minute buckets age out; apps/profile/middleware.py sends seconds left in the 5-minute IP window). Six new tests in apps/reader/test_ratelimit_retry_after.py and apps/profile/test_ip_rate_limit.py. Reply assumes #2146 is merged and deployed with make deploy. PR #2146 went through 14 review rounds at Sam's direction ("keep going, I don't care if it takes 10 rounds"): 25 threads, all fixed and resolved, Codex and Claude clean on head 24b6ea902, Django and Android green, iOS pending at record time. Final shape: on django-redis the decision and count are one Lua call (COUNT_IF_UNDER_LIMIT, EVALSHA via register_script, TTL re-armed if missing); refused requests never write; other backends fall back to incr-then-decr; one refusal log line per key per minute with the folder_rss secret token masked via log_path(); the IP limiter reads the clock once for track_request, the window check and Retry-After. 29 tests across locmem and a real django-redis test class with two real-thread burst tests. Deploy with make deploy only.
13844.reply: Found it. You have 745 saved stories, and every ReadKit sync walks the whole saved list 10 stories at a time, about 75 requests. NewsBlur was allowing 50 requests to the saved stories endpoint in a rolling window of about five minutes, so each sync got cut off with a 429, and ReadKit then retried a minute or two later, which kept you pinned at the limit. Your 30 minute setting is fine, the retries are what made it look constant. I've raised that limit to 100 so a full sync fits, and 429s now say how long to wait, so this should stop with the next sync. I've also written to the ReadKit developer, since fetching 100 saved stories per request on their end would make this go away for larger libraries too.
13844.email:
Subject: NewsBlur 429s in ReadKit saved stories sync

Hi,

I run NewsBlur. A ReadKit user with 745 saved stories posted on our forum about getting 429s on every sync, and I traced it to the saved stories sync. Here is what we see from the server for that account.

Each sync makes about 75 requests to /reader/starred_stories, each returning 10 stories, which is one full pass over the saved list 10 stories at a time. That endpoint was limited to 50 requests per 5 minutes per session, so the pass got cut off around request 50 with a 429. The client then started a new sync 60 to 90 seconds later, which burned whatever budget had freed up, so the account stayed pinned at the limit indefinitely. Over six hours we logged 1,200 saved story requests from this one account, with the feed list and story hash calls every couple of minutes rather than the 30 minutes the user configured.

On our side I've raised that limit to 100 per 5 minutes and the 429 now carries a Retry-After header. Three changes on your side would make this solid for larger libraries, and any one of them would help a lot:

1. Use /reader/starred_story_hashes (with include_timestamps=true) to diff against what you already have, then fetch only the new or changed stories with /reader/starred_stories?h=HASH&h=HASH, up to 100 hashes per request. That is what the hashes endpoint is for and it makes a routine sync a single request.

2. If you keep walking pages, pass limit=100 on /reader/starred_stories. The default is 10. With 100 per page the 745 story library is 8 requests instead of 75.

3. Honor Retry-After on a 429. It says how many seconds until the window frees up, so waiting that long instead of retrying within a minute is enough.

The API docs for both endpoints are at https://newsblur.com/api. Happy to answer questions or test a build against a heavy account.

Sam
